en: Theragāthā 10.1 Dasakanipāta Paṭhamavagga (The First Chapter of the Ten-Fold Collection)
The Verses of the Elder Kāḷudāyi:
“O Venerable One, the trees are now like glowing coals,
having shed their foliage and bearing fruit.”
They shine forth with great radiance like the sun;
O Great Hero, this is the time for you to partake of the flavors.
The trees are in full bloom and enchanting.
They blow from all sides in every direction;
having abandoned the leaf, they hope for fruit.
O Hero, it is time to depart from here.
Neither too cold nor too hot,
O Blessed One, is this pleasant climate for the journey;
let the Sākiyas and the Koḷiyas see you.
One who crosses a river facing downstream while Rohiṇī is in the west plows the field with hope and sows the seed with hope.
Traders set out upon the ocean, carrying wealth, driven by hope;
it is by such hope that I stand.
May this hope of mine be fulfilled.
Again and again they sow the seed;
again and again the King of Gods sends rain.
Again and again the farmers plow the field;
again and again grain comes to the country.
Again and again beggars wander about.
Again and again the givers of gifts give;
having given again and again, the givers of gifts go to the heavenly realm.
The Hero indeed purifies seven generations in whichever family he of vast wisdom is born;
I think that the God of Gods honors that family.
For by her was born the Sage, truly named;
the father of the Great Seer was named Śuddhodana,
while the mother of the Buddha was named Māyā.
Gotamī, who cherished the Bodhisatta within her womb,
now that her body has been broken, rejoices in the world of the Thirty-three;
she has passed away from here and is dead.
Endowed with divine sensual pleasures,
she rejoices in the five strands of sensual pleasure,
surrounded by those hosts of gods.
“I am the son of the Buddha, the conqueror of the unconquerable,
of the peerless Aṅgīrasa, the Tathāgata;
you, Sakka, are my father’s father.”
“By means of the Dhamma, Gotama, you have been my noble kinsman,” said the Elder Kāḷudāyī.
… [The Elder Kāḷudāyī] …
